summary: Groechenig, Wyss and Ziegler prove the Topological Mirror Symmetry conjecture of Hausel and Thaddeus: for coprime d, e and n, the E-polynomial of the moduli space of stable SL_n-Higgs bundles of determinant L of degree d equals the stringy E-polynomial of the PGL_n-moduli stack of degree e twisted by the Hausel–Thaddeus gerbe (Theorem 7.21), with the Hodge-number and fibrewise Galois forms (Corollary 7.22, Theorem 7.23) and a refinement describing the Γ = J_X[n]-isotypic parts (Theorem 7.24). The method is p-adic integration. An orbifold measure on O_F-points of an admissible finite abelian quotient stack computes stringy point counts (Theorem 4.16). A gerbe gives a function f_α equal to the Hasse invariant of its pull-back, computed on the inertia stack (§5, Proposition 5.25, Corollary 5.29). Tate duality then shows that for 'dual abstract Hitchin systems', whose Pryms are dual by a self-dual isogeny and whose torsors are each other's spaces of splittings, the fibrewise p-adic integrals agree (Theorem 6.17), hence stringy point counts agree (Theorem 6.12). An equivariant form of Katz's theorem with fractional Tate twists (Theorems 2.15–2.19) turns these counts into stringy E-polynomials (Theorem 6.11). The same technique shows that point counts of GL_n and SL_n Higgs moduli do not depend on the degree (Theorems 7.15–7.16). The atlas plans the Hitchin fibration along Ngô's route (ET.2b), p-adic measures (LD.2), the local Brauer group and Tate duality (Class field theory Layer 5, R02.4) and algebraic stacks (R09.4–R09.5). The p-adic integration on quotient stacks, the stacky Hasse invariant and the Tate-duality comparison of dual fibrations are the finite-abelian prototype of what PAPER-GROECHENIG-WYSS-ZIEGLER-20-B routes to EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparisonPartII. This route coalesces with it. Stringy invariants, Katz's theorem, abstract Hitchin systems and the SL_n/PGL_n application form a new roadmap. Among the mistakes found: Lemma 5.1's claim that the Galois group of a tame extension splits is false (a cyclic quartic extension of Q_5), Lemma 3.12's Brauer-group form is false (a μ_r-gerbe form is right), Definition 2.16(c) fails for q = 4, and Lemma 2.17 fails with Q_ℓ-coefficients. The main theorems survive.

items.name: Haar measure on F^n
items.statement: For a non-archimedean local field F, F^n is a locally compact abelian group and carries a translation-invariant Haar measure μ_F^n, unique up to a positive scalar and normalised by μ_F^n(O_F^n) = 1.
items.note: Mathlib's haarMeasure K₀ is the left-invariant measure normalised on a positive compact K₀ (haarMeasure_self), and haarMeasure_unique says every σ-finite invariant measure is a multiple of it; K₀ = O_F^n gives μ_F^n.

items.name: The Brauer group of a finite field vanishes
items.statement: Br(k) = 0 for a finite field k; with H²_ét(Spec O_F, G_m) ≅ Br(k_F) this is the input Br(O_F) = 0 used in Lemma 7.19.
items.note: Tau Ceti proves that the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial (Wedderburn); the passage to Br(O_F) by Henselian reduction is part of Lemma 7.19's item.

items.name: The embedding Q/Z ↪ C^× and characters of finite abelian groups
items.statement: Q/Z is viewed inside C^× through λ ↦ e^{2πiλ}; Hasse invariants and Tate pairings are read as complex-valued functions this way, and G^* = Hom(G, Q/Z) is the character group of a finite abelian group G, with |G| = |G^*|.
items.note: AddCircle.toCircle with period 1 is λ ↦ e^{2πiλ} on R/Z; its restriction to Q/Z is the embedding. Pontryagin duals of finite groups are AddChar in Mathlib.

items.name: Finite and finite abelian quotient stacks
items.statement: A Deligne–Mumford stack X is a finite quotient stack if X ≃ [Y/Γ] for an algebraic space Y with a generically fixed-point-free action of an abstract finite group Γ, and a finite abelian quotient stack if Γ can moreover be taken abelian.
items.note: Quotient stacks of algebraic spaces by finite groups belong with the algebraic stacks of R09.4.

items.name: Fermionic shift and weight
items.statement: Let X = [Y/Γ] be a smooth finite quotient stack over a field k with |Γ| invertible in k, and fix a primitive root of unity ζ of order r = ord(γ) in k̄. For a closed point x ∈ Y fixed by γ ∈ Γ, let ζ^{c_1}, …, ζ^{c_k} be the eigenvalues of γ on T_xY with 0 ≤ c_i < r; the fermionic shift is F(γ, x) = Σ c_i/r. It is locally constant on Y^γ and constant on C(γ)-orbits, giving F(γ, ·) : π_0([Y^γ/C(γ)]) → Q. The weight w(γ, ·) is the same sum with 0 < c_i ≤ r; F(γ, Z) = w(γ, Z) − dim Z and w(γ, Z) = dim X − F(γ^{−1}, Z). Both depend on ζ.
items.note: The weight w is the exponent in the volume formula (Theorem 4.16); GWZ20-B's Definition 2.20 generalises it to twisted inertia stacks.

items.name: Inertia stacks of finite quotient stacks
items.statement: For a stack X the inertia stack is IX = X ×_{X×X} X; its S-points are pairs (x, α) with x ∈ X(S) and α ∈ Aut(x), and IX → X is a relative group. For a finite quotient stack, IX ≅ ⊔_{[γ] ∈ Γ/conj} [Y^γ/C(γ)], so F and w are locally constant functions on IX(k)_iso. For a groupoid A with A_iso finite, its mass is #A = Σ_{a ∈ A_iso} 1/|Aut(a)|.
items.note: Inertia stacks and masses of groupoids of points belong with the stacks of R09.4–R09.5, as for GWZ20-B.

items.name: Stringy E-polynomial and stringy point count
items.statement: Let X = [Y/Γ] be a smooth finite quotient stack over a field k, with Y smooth. (a) Over C: E_st(X; x, y) = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ/conj} Σ_{Z ∈ π_0(Y^γ/C(γ))} E(Z; x, y)(xy)^{F(γ,Z)}, where for Z = [W/C(γ)], E(Z; x, y) = Σ_{p,q,k} (−1)^k dim(H^{p,q;k}_c(W)^{C(γ)}) x^p y^q with H^{p,q;k}_c(W) = gr^W_{p+q} H^k_c(W)^{p,q}. (b) Over k = F_q: #_st(X) = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ/conj} Σ_{Z} q^{F(γ,Z)} #Z(k) ∈ R, and #_st(X) = Σ_{x ∈ IX(k)_iso} q^{F(x)}/|Aut_{IX(k)}(x)|. Both are independent of ζ and of the presentation.
items.locator: §2.1, Definition 2.4 and the following paragraph, pp. 513–514; Remark 2.5, p. 514
items.note: Batyrev's stringy invariants for global quotients; the E-polynomial uses Deligne's mixed Hodge structure on compactly supported cohomology.

items.name: Gerbes, bandings and their classification
items.statement: For a Deligne–Mumford stack S and a commutative group scheme A over S, a gerbe over S is a morphism of algebraic stacks α → S whose objects are étale-locally isomorphic and exist étale-locally; an A-banding is a compatible family of isomorphisms A_{S′} ≅ Aut_{S′}(x). A-gerbes up to isomorphism are classified by H²_ét(S, A); automorphisms of an A-gerbe form the groupoid of A-torsors.
items.note: Giraud's classification, as routed for GWZ20-B to R09.4–R09.5.

items.name: Equivariant structures on a trivial gerbe are central extensions
items.statement: Let Y be a scheme with an action of a finite abstract group Γ and A → Y a smooth group scheme. (a) Isomorphism classes of Γ-equivariant structures on the trivial A-gerbe on Y correspond to isomorphism classes of central extensions 1 → A → Γ̂ → Γ → 1 of smooth group Y-schemes. (b) If Γ is cyclic, such Γ̂ is abelian. (c) If Y = Spec k with H²_ét(k, A) = 0 and Γ cyclic, there is a short exact sequence H¹_ét(k, Hom(Γ, A)) ↪ H²_ét([Spec k/Γ], A) ↠ Ext¹(Γ, A_k̄), split when A is constant étale.
items.note: The equivariant structure is a monoidal map Γ → B_Y A; the extension is its pullback of Y → B_Y A.

items.name: Transgression of a gerbe to a torsor on the inertia stack
items.statement: For a Deligne–Mumford stack X and an A-gerbe α → X (A flat commutative), the induced morphism Iα → IX and rigidification by the central A give a central extension 1 → A → ÎX = Iα//A → IX → 1, so P_α := ÎX is an A-torsor on IX. Equivalently: for X = [Y/Γ], the equivariant structure η_γ : γ^*α ≃ α restricted to Y^γ is an automorphism of α|_{Y^γ}, hence a C(γ)-equivariant A-torsor on Y^γ that descends to [Y^γ/C(γ)]; or, via X → B²A, the composite IX → I(B²A) ≃ BA × B²A → BA.
items.note: The three descriptions are asserted to agree; the rigidification is Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli Theorem 5.1.5.

items.name: Transgression of μ_r-gerbes factors through G_m-gerbes
items.statement: Let Y be an irreducible Noetherian scheme with an action of a finite group Γ, covered by Γ-equivariant Zariski-open affines, and r a positive integer with μ_{r·|Γ|} constant étale on Y. Then there is a map τ : H²_ét([Y/Γ], G_m)[r] → H¹_ét(I[Y/Γ], μ_r) with α ↦ P_α equal to τ composed with H²([Y/Γ], μ_r) → H²([Y/Γ], G_m)[r], compatible with β ↦ P_β into H¹(I[Y/Γ], G_m). Equivalently, P_α is trivial when α comes from a line bundle via the Kummer boundary.
items.note: Zariski-locally a line bundle on [Y/Γ] is a character λ : Γ → μ_{|Γ|}, and the extension Γ̂_α is the pullback of 1 → μ_r → μ_{r|Γ|} → μ_{|Γ|} → 1 along λ, which is constant.

items.name: Gerbe-twisted stringy E-polynomial and point count
items.statement: Let X = [Y/Γ] with Y smooth, r ≥ 1 and α ∈ H²_ét(X, μ_r), and let L_γ = P_α|_{[Y^γ/C(γ)]}. (a) Over C: E_st(X, α; x, y) = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ/conj} Σ_{Z ∈ π_0([Y^γ/C(γ)])} E(Z, L_γ; x, y)(xy)^{F(γ,Z)}, where E(Z, L_γ; x, y) = E^χ(L_γ; x, y) is the part of the E-polynomial of the total space of L_γ on the χ-isotypic component for the standard character χ : μ_r(C) ↪ C^×. (b) Over k = F_q with r prime to q, after choosing μ_r(k) ⊂ Q̄_ℓ^×: #^α_st(X) = Σ_γ Σ_Z q^{F(γ,Z)} #^{L_γ}Z(k) with #^{L_γ}Z(k) = Σ_{x ∈ Z(k)_iso} Tr(Fr_x, L_{γ,x})/|Aut(x)|.
items.note: These are the invariants in Hausel–Thaddeus's conjecture.

items.name: Equivariant E-polynomials and χ-twisted point counts
items.statement: For a finite group G, G-varieties are separated G-schemes of finite type with every orbit in an affine open. (a) For a complex G-variety X and a character χ, E^χ_G(X; x, y) = Σ_{p,q,i} (−1)^i dim[gr^{p,q}_W H^i_c(X)^χ] x^p y^q. (b) For a G-variety X over F_q and a Q̄_ℓ-valued character χ, #^χ_G(X) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr[Fr, H^i_{c,ét}(X, Q̄_ℓ)^χ] = Σ_{x ∈ [X/G](F_q)_iso} Tr[Fr_x, (L_χ)_x], with L_χ the local system on [X/G] induced by χ.

items.name: Equivariant Katz theorem: point counts determine E-polynomials
items.statement: Let G be a finite group, R ⊂ C a subalgebra of finite type over Z, fix C ≅ Q̄_ℓ, and let χ be a complex character of G. If X and Y are separated G-schemes of finite type over R with #^χ_G(X ×_R F_q) = #^χ_G(Y ×_R F_q) for every ring homomorphism R → F_q, then E^χ_G(X ×_R C; x, y) = E^χ_G(Y ×_R C; x, y).
items.note: The G-equivariant form of Katz's theorem in the appendix to Hausel–Rodriguez-Villegas (Theorem 6.1.2). The proof reduces to smooth projective X, Y by Bittner's Lemma 7.1, uses purity and Chebotarev density on Spec R[1/ℓ] to identify semisimplified χ-isotypic direct images, and reads off Hodge numbers from Hodge–Tate weights over a finite extension E of Q_ℓ containing R (Fontaine–Messing or Faltings). The printed conclusion names Ω^q for Ω^p (sourceIssues).

items.name: Fractional powers of L and compatible systems of roots of q
items.statement: (a) A compatible system of roots of a prime power q is a sequence s = (s_r) in C with s_1 = q and s_{rr′}^r = s_{r′}. (b) Given R → F_q, a compatible system s extends the χ-twisted point count to #^{s,χ}_{F_q} : K_0(Var_G/R)[(L^{1/r})_{r≥2}] → C by #^{s,χ}(L^{1/r}) = s_r for trivial χ and 0 otherwise. (c) The relation #^χ_{F_q}(X) = #^χ_{F_q}(Y) is asserted to be independent of s. (d) E^χ extends to K_0(Var_G/C)[(L^{1/r})] → Z[(x^{1/r}, y^{1/r})] by E^χ(L^{1/r}) = (xy)^{1/r} for trivial χ and 0 otherwise.
items.note: Part (c) holds for q prime (with the Galois element fixing the values of χ) but fails for q = 4 (sourceIssues).

items.name: Compatible roots of the Tate twist
items.statement: After replacing R by a finite étale extension R′, there are r-th roots Q_ℓ(1/r) of the Tate twist Q_ℓ(1), as lisse ℓ-adic sheaves, for all r ≥ 1, with Q_ℓ(1/(rr′))^{⊗r′} ≅ Q_ℓ(1/r).
items.note: A mild generalisation of Ito's 5.3: restrict the cyclotomic character to an open subgroup U on which log and exp are inverse and take exp((1/r)·log ρ). As stated, with Q_ℓ-coefficients, this fails for high powers of ℓ; it holds for r prime to ℓ and, with Q̄_ℓ-coefficients, for all r (sourceIssues).

items.name: Katz's theorem with fractional Tate twists
items.statement: Let G be a finite group, R ⊂ C of finite type over Z, fix C ≅ Q̄_ℓ and a complex character χ of G. If X, Y ∈ K_0(Var_G/R)[(L^{1/r})_{r≥2}] satisfy #^χ_{F_q}(X) = #^χ_{F_q}(Y) for every R → F_q, then E^χ(X ×_R C; x, y) = E^χ(Y ×_R C; x, y).
items.note: Proof: write X = Σ[X_i]L^{α_i}, Y = Σ[Y_j]L^{β_j} with X_i, Y_j smooth projective and α_i, β_j ∈ Q ∩ [0, 1), compare the lisse sheaves ⊕(R^{c−2α_i}f_{i*}Q_ℓ(α_i))^χ via Chebotarev and read off Hodge–Tate weights. The printed proof has index and sign slips (sourceIssues).

items.name: Stringy point counts determine stringy E-polynomials
items.statement: Let R ⊂ C be of finite type over Z and fix C ≅ Q̄_ℓ. Let X_i be smooth Γ_i-varieties over R for finite abelian groups Γ_1, Γ_2, X_i = [X_i/Γ_i], and α_i a μ_r-gerbe on X_i. If #^{α_1}_st(X_1 ×_R F_q) = #^{α_2}_st(X_2 ×_R F_q) for every R → F_q, then E_st(X_1 ×_R C, α_1; x, y) = E_st(X_2 ×_R C, α_2; x, y).
items.note: Replace both groups by Γ_1 × Γ_2, assume μ_r(C) ⊂ R, realise each L_{i,γ} as the χ-part of the total space Y_{i,γ} of a μ_r-torsor with its Γ × μ_r-action, and apply Theorem 2.18 to Σ_γ[Y_{i,γ}]·L^{F(γ)} (printed as L^{α_i}; sourceIssues).

items.name: Inertia groups, unramified and tamely ramified algebraic extensions
items.statement: For an algebraic extension L of a local field F, the inertia group I_L is the kernel of Gal(L/F) → Gal(k_L/k_F), and e_{L/F} = |I_L| when finite. L/F is totally ramified if k_L = k_F, unramified if every finitely generated intermediate L′ has e_{L′/F} = 1, and tamely ramified if every such e_{L′/F} is prime to p. F ⊂ F^ur ⊂ F^tr ⊂ F^ab ⊂ F^s are the maximal unramified, tamely ramified abelian and abelian extensions.
items.locator: §3.1, Definition 3.1 and the tower following it, pp. 528–529
items.note: The Tau Ceti roadmap Local fields and ramification plans unramified extensions (Layer 2) and ramification, tame and wild (Layer 3).

items.name: Local reciprocity and the unit–valuation diagram
items.statement: The local reciprocity map r : F^× → Gal(F^ab/F) is injective with dense image and fits into a map of split short exact sequences from 0 → O_F^× → F^× → Z → 0 to 0 → Gal(F^ab/F^ur) → Gal(F^ab/F) → Gal(k̄_F/k_F) → 0, the right map sending 1 to the Frobenius x ↦ x^{|k_F|}.
items.note: Local class field theory: the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap plans the local Artin map and its normalisations (Layers 6–7).

items.name: The Brauer group of a local field
items.statement: inv : Br(F) ≅ Q/Z, and for a finite extension L/F the restriction Br(F) → Br(L) corresponds to multiplication by [L : F].
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 plans the Brauer group, invMap and the degree-multiplying restriction square.

items.name: Local Tate duality for finite modules and the Euler characteristic
items.statement: For a commutative finite group scheme M over F of order prime to p, cup product and inv give a perfect pairing H^i_ét(F, M) × H^{2−i}_ét(F, M^∨) → Q/Z with M^∨ = Hom(M, G_m); H^i vanishes for i ≥ 3; and |H¹_ét(F, M)| = |M(F)|·|M^∨(F)|.
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 plans local Tate duality for the evaluation pairing, finiteness of H⁰, H¹, H² and the cardinality Euler characteristic. The unramified-orthogonality clause of Theorem 3.3 is part of the next item.

items.name: Torsors under a constant group over a local field and their Tate pairing
items.statement: Let Γ be a finite abelian group of order prime to p and π ∈ F a uniformiser. Composition with Z × μ(F) → F^× (1 ↦ π, inclusion on μ(F)) and the reciprocity map gives an isomorphism H¹_ét(F, Γ) ≅ Γ ⊕ Hom(μ(F), Γ), under which Γ is the unramified part H¹_ur(F, Γ) (Proposition 3.6). Under Tate duality H^i_ur(F, M) and H^{2−i}_ur(F, M^∨) are exact annihilators (Theorem 3.3, second part). If F contains the |Γ|-th roots of unity, then Γ^∨ is constant with value Hom(Γ, μ(F)), and the Tate pairing of H¹(F, Γ) with H¹(F, Γ^∨) pairs the first factors with each other and the second factors with each other trivially, and is otherwise the evaluation pairings Γ × Hom(μ(F), Hom(Γ, μ(F))) → Hom(μ(F), μ(F)) ≅ Z/|μ(F)| and Hom(μ(F), Γ) × Hom(Γ, μ(F)) → Z/|μ(F)| (Lemma 3.7).
items.locator: §3.1, Theorem 3.3 (second part), Construction 3.5, Proposition 3.6, Lemma 3.7, pp. 530–532
items.note: Uses O_F^× ≅ (free Z_p-module) ⊕ μ(F) (Neukirch II.5.7) and Milne ADT I.2.5(b); GWZ20-B's unramified and strongly ramified torsors (its Lemmas 2.14–2.16) are the non-split version.

items.name: Tate duality for abelian varieties over a local field
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over F: H^r_ét(F, A^∨) ≅ Ext^{r+1}_F(A, G_m) functorially in A (Milne I.3.1, Lemma 3.8); Yoneda composition with H²(F, G_m) ≅ Q/Z gives functorial pairings H^r(F, A) × H^{1−r}(F, A^∨) → Q/Z (Construction 3.9); H^r(F, A) = 0 for r ≥ 2, A(F) is profinite, H¹(F, A) is torsion of cofinite type, and for r = 0, 1 the pairing is continuous and non-degenerate (Tate; Theorem 3.10). Under H¹(F, A^∨) ≅ Ext²(A, G_m) ≅ Hom_D(A, G_m[2]) a torsor T is a G_m-gerbe α_T on A, and the pairing of a ∈ A(F) with T is inv(a^*α_T) (Remark 3.11).
items.note: Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems, I.3.1–I.3.4 and I.0; routed to R02.4 as for GWZ20-B.

items.name: Arithmetic gerbes with a group structure on abelian varieties and torsors
items.statement: Let F be a local field, r invertible in F, A/F an abelian variety and P/F an A-torsor. The natural map Ext²(A, μ_r) → H²_ét(A, μ_r) is injective, with image the μ_r-gerbes trivial on A_{F^s} and along the unit section e (Lemma 3.12, first part); Ext²(A, μ_r) ≅ H¹(F, A^∨[r]). The paper further asserts ker(Br(P) → Br(P_{F^s}))[r]/Br(F)[r] ≃ Ext²(A, μ_r) (Lemma 3.12, second part) and ker(Br(A) → Br(A_{F^s}))[r]/Br(F)[r] ≃ ker(Br(P) → Br(P_{F^s}))[r]/Br(F)[r] (Corollary 3.13).
items.note: The Brauer-group forms are false as printed and hold with H²_ét(−, μ_r) in place of Br(−)[r] (sourceIssues); that corrected form is what Lemma 6.7 uses.

items.name: The long exact sequence of an isogeny is self-dual under Tate duality
items.statement: For an isogeny φ : A → B of abelian varieties over F, 0 → ker φ → A → B → 0 gives 0 → ker(φ)(F) → A(F) → B(F) → H¹(F, ker φ) → H¹(F, A) → H¹(F, B) → H²(F, ker φ) → 0 (Construction 3.14), and Tate duality identifies it, term by term and compatibly with the boundary maps, with the Pontryagin dual of the sequence of φ^∨ : B^∨ → A^∨ with ker(φ^∨) ≅ ker(φ)^∨ (Lemma 3.15).
items.note: Compatibility with boundary maps is checked on the Ext pairings Ext^i(C, G_m) × H^{2−i}(F, C) → Q/Z as Yoneda compositions.

items.name: Self-dual isogenies over a local field
items.statement: An isogeny φ : A → B is self-dual if there is ψ : A ≅ B^∨ with ψ^∨∘φ = φ^∨∘ψ; then ker(φ)^∨ ≅ ker(φ^∨) ≅ ker(φ) (12). If φ is a self-dual isogeny over F whose kernel has order prime to p, then |B(F)/φ(A(F))| = |ker(φ)(F)|.
items.note: K = B(F)/φ(A(F)) and Q = H¹(F, ker φ)/K are dual by Lemma 3.15, so |H¹(F, ker φ)| = |K|²; Theorem 3.4 with ker φ ≅ (ker φ)^∨ gives |H¹(F, ker φ)| = |ker(φ)(F)|².

items.name: The measure of an r-gauge form on an F-analytic manifold
items.statement: For an n-dimensional F-analytic manifold X and a global section ω of (Ω^n_X)^{⊗r}, on a compact open chart U ↪ F^n with ω|_U = f(x)(dx_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx_n)^{⊗r} set μ_ω(U) = ∫_U |f|^{1/r} dμ^n_F; this extends to a measure on X (Yasuda 3.2). A nowhere-vanishing section of (Ω^top_X)^{⊗r} is an r-gauge form. Smooth F-varieties give F-manifolds X(F), and algebraic forms give analytic ones.
items.note: As routed for GWZ20-B's Section 2.1 to LD.2.

items.name: Fubini along a submersion and change of variables
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a submersion of F-manifolds and ω_X, ω_Y r-gauge forms. There is a unique analytic section θ of (Ω^top_f)^{⊗r} with θ ∧ f^*ω_Y = ω_X under f^*Ω^top_Y ⊗ Ω^top_f ≅ Ω^top_X, and for integrable α, ∫_X α dμ_{ω_X} = ∫_Y (∫_{f^{−1}(y)} α dμ_{θ_y}) dμ_{ω_Y}; θ is algebraic when f comes from a smooth morphism and the forms are algebraic (Proposition 4.1). Locally every r-gauge form has |η^{⊗r}| = q^m|ω| for a 1-gauge form η and m ∈ Q (Claim 4.2). For an isomorphism f : X → Y and integrable α, ∫_X α∘f dμ_{f^*ω_Y} = ∫_Y α dμ_{ω_Y} (Lemma 4.3).
items.note: The r = 1 case is Igusa, Theorem 7.6.1 and §7.4. Claim 4.2's proof names the wrong form (sourceIssues).

items.name: Yasuda's measure on O_F-points: null sets and change of variables
items.statement: For an O_F-variety X, X° = X(O_F) ∩ X_F^sm(F) is an F-manifold and a section of (Ω^top_{X/F})^{⊗r} on X_F^sm gives a measure on X(O_F), extended by zero. (1) μ_ω(Y(O_F)) = 0 for every subscheme Y ⊂ X of positive codimension. (2) If f : Y → X is Γ-invariant for a generically stabiliser-free action of a finite group Γ on Y with Y/Γ → X birational, then (1/|Γ|)∫_A |f^*ω|^{1/r} = ∫_{f(A)} |ω|^{1/r} for every open Γ-invariant A ⊂ Y(O_F) and r-gauge form ω on X°.
items.note: Yasuda, Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.8; as GWZ20-B's Proposition 2.1.

items.name: Weil's formula for the volume of O_F-points
items.statement: For a smooth O_F-scheme X of relative dimension d with its canonical measure, vol(X(O_F)) = #X(k_F)/q^d.
items.locator: §1, equation (1), p. 510; used in the proofs of Theorems 7.15–7.16, pp. 583–586
items.note: Weil's canonical measure; routed to LD.2 as GWZ20-B's Theorem 1.4.

items.name: Twisting by torsors
items.statement: Let S be a scheme and Γ a commutative étale group S-scheme. For an S-scheme N with a Γ-action and T ∈ H¹_ét(S, Γ), the T-twist is the algebraic space N_T = [(N ×_S T)/Γ] (anti-diagonal action), with Γ acting through T (Definition 4.5). There is an equivalence [N/Γ] ≃ [N_T/Γ] (Lemma 4.6), proved by exchanging quotients: for commuting actions of fppf group schemes Γ_1, Γ_2, [[N/Γ_1]/Γ_2] ≃ [[N/Γ_2]/Γ_1] (Lemma 4.7).
items.note: Quotient-stack identities for twisted actions, routed to R09.4 as GWZ20-B's Construction 5.1.

items.name: Frobenius on the cohomology of twists and point counts of quotient stacks
items.statement: For a variety U over a finite field k with an action of a finite abelian group Γ and a Γ-torsor T ∈ H¹(k, Γ) = Γ corresponding to γ, there is an isomorphism H^i_ét(U, Q̄_ℓ) ≅ H^i_ét(U_T, Q̄_ℓ) under which Fr_{U_T} = (γ^*)^{−1}·Fr_U (Proposition 4.8). For a smooth variety M over k with a Γ-action, |[M/Γ](k)| = (1/|Γ|)Σ_{T ∈ H¹(k,Γ)} |M_T(k)| (Corollary 4.9).
items.note: As GWZ20-B's unramified twists and their isotypic decomposition.

items.name: Admissible finite abelian quotient stacks
items.statement: A ring R contains all roots of unity of order m if μ_m(R) surjects onto μ_m(k̄) for every R → k̄ algebraically closed. A finite abelian quotient stack M over R is admissible if M ≅ [Y/Γ] with Y a smooth quasi-projective R-variety, Γ a finite abelian group acting generically fixed-point-freely, |Γ| invertible in R, and R containing all roots of unity of order |Γ|; M = Y/Γ is its geometric quotient. Then M is Q-Gorenstein (Lemma 4.11).
items.note: Normality from Mumford's GIT 0.2(2); Q-Cartier Weil divisors from Kollár–Mori Lemma 5.16.

items.name: The orbifold measure
items.statement: For M = [Y/Γ] admissible over O_F with pr : Y → M, Δ ⊂ Y the non-free locus and U = Y ∖ Δ, let M(O_F)^♮ = M(O_F) ∩ pr(U)(F). There is a unique Q-Weil divisor D on M with K_M + D Q-Cartier and pr^*(K_M + D) = K_Y (Yasuda, Lemma 7.2); for r with r(K_M + D) Cartier, the line bundle I is a subsheaf of (Ω^top_{pr(U)})^{⊗r} over pr(U), and integrating local generators of I defines μ_orb on M(O_F)^♮, extended by zero, independent of the presentation (Construction 4.12). If Ω^top_Y has a nowhere-vanishing ω, then Nm(ω) = ⊗_γ γ^*ω descends to ω_orb with pr^*ω_orb = Nm(ω) computing μ_orb (Remark 4.13); if codim_Y Δ ≥ 2 and Ω^top_{pr(U)} is trivialised by ω, then μ_orb(A) = ∫_A |ω| (Remark 4.14).
items.note: Yasuda's measure for the pair (M, D), Definition 4.7; GWZ20-B's canonical measure on coarse spaces of tame DM stacks generalises it.

items.name: The specialisation map to the inertia stack
items.statement: For φ ∈ M(O_F)^♮, let T_φ be the fibre of Y → M over φ_F, a Γ-torsor over F with Γ(T_φ) = L^{×i} for a finite Galois L/F, and O_{T_φ} = O_L^{×i}. The inclusion T_φ → Y extends uniquely (valuative criterion for the finite map pr, separatedness of Y) to a Γ-equivariant φ̃ : Spec O_{T_φ} → Y, giving [Spec O_{T_φ}/Γ] → M whose closed point has stabiliser I_{L/F}. I_{L/F} is cyclic with a canonical surjection μ(F) ↠ I_{L/F}, so the chosen primitive |Γ|-th root of unity gives a generator γ, and (Aut_x → IM_{k_F}, γ) defines e : M(O_F)^♮ → IM(k_F)_iso.
items.note: GWZ20-B's specialisation map to the twisted inertia stack generalises it. The generator must come from the tame character I_{L/F} ≅ μ_e, not from the reciprocity map as printed (sourceIssues).

items.name: Volume of the fibres of the specialisation map
items.statement: Let M = [Y/Γ] be an admissible finite abelian quotient stack over O_F. For every γ ∈ Γ and x ∈ [Y^γ/Γ](k_F) ⊂ IM(k_F), μ_orb(e^{−1}(x)) = q^{−w(γ,x)}/|Aut(x)|. (Theorem 1.5 of the introduction: for X a smooth O_F-scheme with a generically free Γ-action as above, vol(X/Γ(O_F)^♮) computed by the orbifold measure equals q^{−dim X}#_st([X/Γ] ×_{O_F} k_F).)
items.note: Reduces to the cyclic case by Proposition 4.4 over Y/I → Y/Γ with I = ⟨γ⟩, using |Aut(x)| = |Γ|/|s_γ^{−1}(x)|. The special case of GWZ20-B's stacky Weil formula for finite abelian quotients.

items.name: The affine and cyclic cases of the volume formula
items.statement: (Proposition 4.17) If M = A^n, Γ = ⟨γ⟩ cyclic of order d acts by γ·(x_i) = (ζ^{c_i}x_i) with 1 ≤ c_i ≤ d, and 0 is the image of the origin in [(A^n)^γ/Γ](k_F), then μ_orb(e^{−1}(0)) = q^{−w(γ,0)}/d; the proof uses λ : A^n → A^n/Γ, f(x) ↦ f(π^{c_1/d}x_1, …, π^{c_n/d}x_n), whose image on O_F-points is e^{−1}(0) (Denef–Loeser (2.3.4)), with λ^*ω_orb = π^{Σc_i}(dx_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx_n)^{⊗d}. (Proposition 4.18) For Γ cyclic of order d and Y any smooth O_F-variety as in Theorem 4.16, μ_orb(e^{−1}(x)) = q^{−w(γ,x)}/d for every x ∈ [Y^γ/Γ](k_F).
items.locator: §4.3, Propositions 4.17–4.18, pp. 544–545, and their proofs, p. 546
items.note: Proposition 4.18 follows from 4.17 by Lemma 4.19, after an unramified twist (Lemma 4.6) when x does not lift to Y^γ(k_F).

items.name: Equivariant étale linearisation at a fixed point
items.statement: Let x ∈ Y(k_F) be a closed point fixed by Γ (|Γ| prime to p). There are a Γ-invariant open U ∋ x and an étale f : U → A^n_{O_F} such that (i) f is Γ-equivariant for a diagonal Γ-action on A^n, and (ii) f induces an F-analytic isomorphism {φ ∈ (Y/Γ)(O_F) : φ|_{k_F} = x} → {φ ∈ (A^n/Γ)(O_F) : φ|_{k_F} = 0}.
items.note: Average an étale chart f′ (Milne, Étale cohomology, Proposition I.3.24) as f = Σ_γ A_γ^{−1}∘f′∘γ, whose differential at x is |Γ|·df′; (ii) is Hensel's lemma.

items.name: Tame Galois extensions of a local field containing the e-th roots of unity
items.statement: Let L/F be a finite Galois extension of degree d with ramification index e = |I|, I = I_{L/F}, tame ((p, e) = 1), with μ_e ⊂ F, and Γ = Gal(L/F). Lemma 5.1 asserts: (a) for a uniformiser π_L of L, F(π_L) is totally ramified, Galois and of degree e over F, and Gal(L/F(π_L)) maps isomorphically to Γ/I; (b) Γ/I ≅ Z/(d/e) and I ≅ μ_e(F); (c) Γ is abelian and a split extension of Z/(d/e) by Z/e, so F(π_L) gives Γ ≅ (Γ/I) × I; (d) every splitting of Γ → Γ/I arises from a uniformiser in this way.
items.note: Γ is abelian and I ≅ μ_e canonically by σ ↦ σ(π_L)/π_L mod m_L (the Tau Ceti roadmap Local fields and ramification, Layer 3, plans the tame structure theorem and Gal ↪ μ_e). Parts (a), (c), (d) are false in general: Γ need not split (sourceIssues); it does after replacing L by its compositum with the unramified extension of degree d, which leaves X_{L/F} unchanged.

items.name: The stack X_{L/F} and its closed and open points
items.statement: X_{L/F} = [Spec O_L/Γ] (Definition 5.2). For a finite étale Galois X → Y with group G, [X/G] ≃ Y (Lemma 5.3), so Spec F = [Spec L/Γ] gives an open immersion i_F : Spec F ↪ X_{L/F} (Lemma 5.4), and X_{F(π_L)/F} ≃ X_{L/F} for a uniformiser as in Lemma 5.1 (Lemma 5.5). The reduced closed complement is X^•_{L/F} (Definition 5.6), and each splitting σ : Γ → I of I ↪ Γ gives X^•_{L/F} = [Spec k_L/Γ] ≃ B_{k_F}I and a closed immersion j_σ : B_{k_F}I ↪ X_{L/F} (Lemma 5.7).
items.note: GWZ20-B's stacks X_{Γ,Q} = [Q_O/Γ] with Bμ_N ↪ X_{Γ,Q} generalise this. X^•_{L/F} ≃ B_{k_F}I holds for every L; the printed proof takes the splitting from Lemma 5.1 (sourceIssues).

items.name: Cohomology of X_{L/F}
items.statement: Pic(X_{L/F}) ≅ Z/eZ, via H¹(I, O_{F(π_L)}^×) ≅ H¹(I, k_F^×) ≅ Hom(μ_e, G_m) (Lemma 5.8, Claim 5.9). For a finite étale sheaf F of order prime to p and every splitting σ, j_σ^* : H^i_ét(X_{L/F}, F) ≅ H^i_ét(B_{k_F}I, F) for i = 0, 1, 2 (Lemma 5.10), because pullback along Spec k_L ↪ Spec O_L is an equivalence of 2-groupoids of F-gerbes (Claim 5.11). There is a split short exact sequence Z/e ↪ H²_ét(B_{k_F}I, μ_e) ↠ Z/e (Lemma 5.12), hence, given σ, Z/e ↪ H²_ét(X_{L/F}, μ_e) ↠ Z/e (Lemma 5.13, (18)).
items.note: Lemma 5.8 uses H^i(I, 1 + m) = 0, since e is invertible on the pro-p group 1 + m; Lemma 5.12 is Lemma 2.7(c), misquoted in the printed proof (sourceIssues). GWZ20-B's Lemma 3.4 computes H² of Bμ_N over a field in the same way.

items.name: The Brauer group of X_{L/F}
items.statement: i_F^*α has order dividing d because Br(O_L) = 0 and restriction to L is multiplication by d (Theorem 3.2); i_F^* : Br(X_{L/F}) → Br(F)[d] is injective, by the Brauer–Severi construction and the valuative criterion (Lemma 5.14); and i_F^* : Br(X_{L/F}) ≅ Br(F)[e], so Br(X_{L/F}) has order e (Proposition 5.15). For a finite group Γ acting on a scheme U with an ample invertible sheaf, Br([U/Γ]) ≅ H²_ét([U/Γ], G_m)^tors (Lemma 5.16), using α-twisted coherent sheaves (Definition 5.17) and Gabber–de Jong. For every splitting σ, j_σ^* : Br(X_{L/F})[e] ≅ Br(B_{k_F}I)[e] (Proposition 5.18, (19)), independently of σ (Lemma 5.19).
items.note: The proof of Lemma 5.14 misstates the Brauer–Severi dictionary, and the proof of Proposition 5.18 omits the order of Br(B_{k_F}I)[e] (sourceIssues).

items.name: Transgression computes the Hasse invariant
items.statement: Assume μ_{e²} ⊂ k_F. Let τ : Br(B_{k_F}I)[e] → H¹_ét(IB_{k_F}I, μ_e) be the transgression of Lemma 2.9, IB_{k_F}I ≃ I × B_{k_F}I, and Tr : H¹_ét(IB_{k_F}I, μ_e) → Hom(μ_e, H¹_ét(k_F, μ_e)) ≅ Z/e the pullback along Spec k_F × I → IB_{k_F}I (20) followed by evaluation at Frobenius (21); τ̃ = Tr∘τ∘j_σ^* : Br(X_{L/F}) → Z/e is independent of σ. Then τ̃∘(i_F^*)^{−1} = inv on Br(F)[e] (Theorem 5.20, with Claim 5.21).
items.note: The proof represents α by (π^{φ_ijk}) on the unramified site, splits α_L by (π^{ψ_ij/e}) with dψ = eφ, and reads off the cocycle ξ ↦ ξ^{ψ_ij}. GWZ20-B's Proposition 3.7 is the general form. The identification with τ̃ is asserted, not proved, and there are slips in the Bockstein step (sourceIssues).

items.name: Admissible gerbes and the transgression function
items.statement: For an admissible finite abelian quotient stack M over R: r ≥ 1 is admissible for M if r is invertible in R and R contains the r·|Γ|-th roots of unity for some admissible presentation [Y/Γ]; a G_m-gerbe is admissible if its order is finite and admissible; a μ_r-gerbe is admissible if r is (Definition 5.22). Situation 5.23: M admissible over O_F with coarse space M and U ⊂ M the maximal open over which M → M is an isomorphism; a proper O_F-scheme Y with i : Y → M sending Y_F into U; an admissible G_m-gerbe α on M with inv_α(y) = inv(y^*α) on M(O_F)^♮. For α ∈ Br(M_{k_F})[r], τ_α : IM(k_F)_iso → Z/r is defined by ζ^{τ_α(y)} = y^*τ(α) ∈ H¹(k_F, μ_r) = μ_r (Definition 5.24).

items.name: The Hasse invariant of a gerbe is read off at the specialisation
items.statement: For M an admissible finite abelian quotient stack over O_F and α an admissible G_m-gerbe on M: inv_α = τ_α∘e_M on M(O_F)^♮ (Proposition 5.25). In Situation 5.23, inv_α = τ_α∘e_M∘i on Y(F) (Corollary 5.26).
items.note: [Spec O_{T_φ}/Γ] ≅ X_{L/F} and Theorem 5.20. The published proof of Corollary 5.26 uses i(y) ∈ U(F) to land in M(O_F)^♮; arXiv v3's weaker hypothesis did not suffice. GWZ20-B's Proposition 3.7 and Corollary 3.14 are the general forms. The application of Theorem 5.20 needs μ_{e²} ⊂ k_F, which admissibility does not give (sourceIssues).

items.name: The gerbe function f_α
items.statement: Let r ≥ 1 be prime to p with μ_r ⊂ F, fix a generator ζ ∈ μ_r(F), an isomorphism Q̄_ℓ ≅ C and hence ι : μ_r(F) ↪ Q̄_ℓ^×. For M admissible over O_F and α an admissible μ_r-gerbe, L_α is the ℓ-adic local system on I(M ×_{O_F} k) induced by P_α and ι (Definition 5.27), and f_α : M(O_F)^♮ → C, x ↦ Tr_{Fr_{e(x)}}(L_α|_{e(x)}) (23), agrees with τ_α∘e_M under the exponential and, by Proposition 5.25, with x ↦ exp(2πi·inv(x^*α)) (Construction 5.28).
items.note: The sign of the exponent depends on whether Fr is the arithmetic or the geometric Frobenius, which the paper does not fix; both sides of every later comparison change together.

items.name: Twisted stringy point counts as p-adic integrals
items.statement: For M an admissible finite abelian quotient stack over O_F and α an admissible μ_r-gerbe on M: #^α_st(M_{k_F})/q^{dim M} = ∫_{M(O_F)^♮} f̄_α dμ_orb = ∫_{M(O_F)^♮} exp(−2πi·inv_α) dμ_orb.
items.note: Theorem 4.16 gives ∫ f_α dμ_orb as a sum over the sectors of q^{−w(γ,Z)} = q^{F(γ^{−1},Z)−dim M} times traces; L_α|_{[Y^γ/Γ]} = L_α^{−1}|_{[Y^{γ^{−1}}/Γ]} by (2), and re-indexing γ ↦ γ^{−1} gives the complex conjugate of the stringy count.

items.name: Arithmetic gerbes and relative splittings
items.statement: Let U → V be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces with geometrically connected fibres, r invertible on V, Pic̃(U/V) the stack of line bundles, Pic(U/V) its G_m-rigidification and Pic^τ(U/V) the open substack of line bundles of torsion degree on geometric fibres. For a smooth group scheme A over V, an A-gerbe α on U is V-arithmetic if it splits on U ×_V V_i for an étale cover {V_i → V} (Definition 6.1). For a G_m-gerbe α, Split̃(U/V, α) sends W → V to the groupoid of splittings of α on U ×_V W; it is a Pic̃(U/V)-pseudotorsor, and a torsor when α is V-arithmetic (Lemma 6.2). For α ∈ H²(U, μ_r), Split̃_{μ_r}(U/V, α) is the stack of μ_r-splittings and Split_{μ_r} its μ_r-rigidification (Definition 6.3); Tors_{μ_r} ≃ Pic̃(U/V)[r] after rigidification, and for V-arithmetic α the principal component is the Pic^τ(U/V)-torsor Split′(U/V, α) = Split_{μ_r}(U/V, α) ×^{Pic(U/V)[r]} Pic^τ(U/V) (Definition 6.4).
items.note: Pic̃(U/V) is Artin's algebraic stack of line bundles; rigidification is Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli §5.

items.name: Rational points of the principal component and constant gerbes
items.statement: For a field K and a projective geometrically connected K-scheme X, a G_m-gerbe β on X is K-arithmetic iff β_{K^s} = 0; write Br(X)_K for these. The paper records a short exact sequence 0 → Br(K) → Br(X)_K → H¹(K, Pic(X_{K^s})) → 0 (24). If K is a field, X geometrically connected and proper, α a K-arithmetic μ_r-gerbe on X with induced G_m-gerbe β, and Split′(X, α) has a K-point, then β is the pullback of a G_m-gerbe on Spec K (Lemma 6.5). A splitting of α gives a K-point of Split′, but not conversely: if α is pulled back from a non-split gerbe on Spec K and X(K) ≠ ∅, α does not split while Split′(X, α) ≃ Pic^τ(X) has a K-point.
items.locator: §6.1, (24), the paragraph before Lemma 6.5 and Lemma 6.5, pp. 565–566
items.note: Lemma 6.5 uses only exactness of (24) in the middle, which is the Hochschild–Serre sequence; the injectivity and surjectivity printed in (24) fail in general (sourceIssues).

items.name: Unitary splittings
items.statement: For a smooth projective morphism U → V of complex varieties and a V-arithmetic μ_r-gerbe α on U with Pic^τ(U/V) = Pic^0(U/V), the complex space Split′(U/V, α) is isomorphic to the manifold of flat unitary splittings of the unitary gerbe induced by α (Hausel–Thaddeus §3).
items.note: Not used in the proofs; it translates Split′ into Hausel–Thaddeus's Triv.

items.name: The gerbe function on a torsor is a Tate character
items.statement: In Situation 5.23 with Y_F a torsor under an abelian variety A over F and α an O_F-arithmetic μ_r-gerbe, T = Split′(Y/O_F, α) has generic fibre an A^∨-torsor. If Y_F(F) ≠ ∅, then for every trivialisation h : Y_F ≅ A there is a root of unity ξ with f_α∘h^{−1}(a) = ξ·exp(2πi(a, [T_F])) on A(F), where f_α is the function of (23) and (−, −) : A(F) × H¹(F, A^∨) → Q/Z is the Tate pairing.
items.note: For Y_F = A with h = id: Lemma 3.12 gives α = α_T, Remark 3.11 identifies (x, T) with inv(x^*α_T), and Corollary 5.26 identifies f_α with inv(x^*α). A general trivialisation changes α by a constant Brauer class (Corollary 3.13, in its corrected μ_r-form), whence ξ.

items.name: Abstract Hitchin systems
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring. (M, P, A) is an abstract Hitchin system over R if A/R is a smooth R-variety, M is a smooth admissible finite abelian quotient stack over R with π : M → A, and P is an A-group scheme acting on M over A, such that for some open dense A^♦ ⊂ A: (a) the coarse space M → A is proper; (b) P^♦ = P ×_A A^♦ is an abelian A^♦-scheme; (c) there is an open dense M′ ⊂ M that is a P-torsor over A (not necessarily surjective over A), with M^♦ = M ×_A A^♦ ⊂ M′ and codim(M ∖ M′) ≥ 2. Then M is generically a scheme.
items.locator: §6.2, Definition 6.8 and the paragraph after it, p. 568
items.note: Modelled on Ngô's G-Hitchin system, §4.

items.name: Dual pairs of abstract Hitchin systems
items.statement: A dual pair over R is two abstract Hitchin systems (M_i, P_i, A), i = 1, 2, with admissible A-arithmetic μ_r-gerbes α_i on M_i, and an open dense A^♦ ⊂ A satisfying Definition 6.8 for both, such that: (a) there is an étale isogeny φ : P_1 → P_2 of group A-schemes, with the orders of the geometric fibres of ker φ over A^♦ invertible in R in positive or mixed characteristic; (b) over A^♦ there is ψ : (P_1^♦)^∨ ≅ P_2^♦ making φ self-dual; (c) with i′ the other index, Split′(M_i^♦/A^♦, α_i) is a (P_i^♦)^∨-torsor, hence a P_{i′}^♦-torsor via (b), and there are isomorphisms of torsors Split′(M_i^♦/A^♦, α_i) ≃ M_{i′}^♦; (d) for every local field F, every R → O_F and every a ∈ A(O_F) ∩ A^♦(F), both fibres π_1^{−1}(a_F), π_2^{−1}(a_F) have F-points iff both α_1|_{π_1^{−1}(a_F)} and α_2|_{π_2^{−1}(a_F)} split; (e) r is invertible in R and R contains all r-th roots of unity. Condition (c) gives the 'if' half of (d). Dual pairs base change along R → R′. (Definition 1.2 of the introduction is condition (c).)
items.locator: §6.2, Definition 6.9 and Remark 6.10, pp. 568–569; §1, Definition 1.2, p. 508
items.note: Condition (c) is printed with 'P_i^♦-torsors' where P_{i′}^♦ is meant, and Definition 1.2 repeats α_2 (sourceIssues).

items.name: Topological mirror symmetry for dual abstract Hitchin systems
items.statement: Let R ⊂ C be a subalgebra of finite type over Z and (M_i, P_i, A, α_i) a dual pair of abstract Hitchin systems over R. Then E_st(M_1 ×_R C, α_1) = E_st(M_2 ×_R C, α_2).
items.note: Deduced from Theorem 6.12 by Theorem 2.19.

items.name: Arithmetic mirror symmetry for dual abstract Hitchin systems
items.statement: Let k be a finite field and (M_i, P_i, A, α_i) a dual pair over k. Then #^{α_1}_st(M_1) = #^{α_2}_st(M_2), and fibrewise: for every a ∈ A(k), Tr(Fr, (Rπ^I_{1,*}N_{α_1}(F_1))_a) = Tr(Fr, (Rπ^I_{2,*}N_{α_2}(F_2))_a), where π^I_i : IM_i → A, N_{α_i} is the ℓ-adic local system on IM_i from the transgressed μ_r-torsor and a fixed μ_r(k) ↪ Q̄_ℓ^×, and N_{α_i}(F_i) is its Tate twist by the fermionic shift.
items.note: Proof: over F = k((t)), write each fibrewise trace by the Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula as q^{dim M_i}Σ_x q^{−w_i(x)}·conj(Tr(Fr, L_{α_i,x}))/|Aut(x)| (using F_i(x) = dim M_i − w_i(ι(x)) for the inversion ι of IM_i), turn it into ∫ f̄_{α_i} dμ_orb by Theorem 4.16, discard A(O_F) ∖ A(O_F)^♭ (Proposition 4.4), apply Fubini (Proposition 4.1) along the smooth M_i^♦ → A^♦, and compare fibres by Theorem 6.17.

items.name: Invariant gauge forms on torsors
items.statement: Let V be a scheme, A → V a smooth group V-scheme with zero section s, and T → V an A-torsor with structure map q. There is a canonical isomorphism q^*s^*Ω^m_{A/V} ≅ Ω^m_{T/V}.
items.note: For T = A extend by left-invariant forms (Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron models 4.2.2); in general descend from a trivialising cover, the choice being invisible to invariant forms.

items.name: Gauge forms on an abstract Hitchin system and the orbifold measure
items.statement: Over F = k((t)), near a ∈ A(k) fix a volume form ω_A on A and a translation-invariant generator ω̃_2 of Ω^top_{P_2/A}; ω̃_1 = φ^*ω̃_2 generates Ω^top_{P_1/A} since ker φ has order prime to p. Via Lemma 6.13, ω̃_i gives a relative form on the P_i-torsor M′_i, π^*ω_A ∧ ω̃_i is a nowhere-vanishing top form on M′_i, and by condition (c) of Definition 6.8 and Hartogs it extends to a nowhere-vanishing ω_i on M_i, so μ_orb,i on M_i(O_F)^♮ is ∫|ω_i| (Remark 4.14, as M′_i has no orbifold points). For b ∈ A(O_F)^♭ = A(O_F) ∩ A^♦(F), ω̃_{i,b} is the volume form on the fibres of M_i and P_i over b. Condition (c) is necessary: blowing up a point outside M′_i keeps the other hypotheses but breaks Theorem 6.12.
items.note: Remark 6.14 compares this use of condition (c) to the Calabi–Yau condition in Batyrev's argument.

items.name: Key Lemma: dual fibres have equal volumes
items.statement: Let (M_i, P_i, A, α_i) be a dual pair over O_F and b ∈ A(O_F)^♭ with π_i^{−1}(b)(F) ≠ ∅ for i = 1, 2. Then ∫_{π_1^{−1}(b)(F)} |ω̃_{1,b}| = ∫_{π_2^{−1}(b)(F)} |ω̃_{2,b}|.
items.note: Each fibre is a trivial P_{i,b}-torsor; Proposition 4.4 gives (1/|ker φ(F)|)∫_{P_{1,b}(F)}|ω̃_{1,b}| = ∫_{φ(P_{1,b}(F))}|ω̃_{2,b}|, translation invariance gives the index |P_{2,b}(F)/φ(P_{1,b}(F))|, and Proposition 3.16 equates the two. The authors' GWZ18 gives an alternative Néron-model argument.

items.name: p-adic mirror symmetry for dual abstract Hitchin systems
items.statement: For every b ∈ A(O_F)^♭: ∫_{π_1^{−1}(b)(F)} f_{α_1}|ω̃_{1,b}| = ∫_{π_2^{−1}(b)(F)} f_{α_2}|ω̃_{2,b}|. (Theorem 1.6 of the introduction.)
items.locator: §6.3, Theorem 6.17 and its proof, pp. 573–574; §1, Theorem 1.6, p. 510
items.note: Four cases: both fibres empty; exactly one empty, where by Lemma 6.7 f_{α_2}∘h^{−1} is a constant times the non-trivial character exp(2πi(−, t_1)) with t_1 = [π_1^{−1}(b)] ≠ 0, so the integral vanishes by translation invariance; both non-empty, where condition (d) and Proposition 5.25 give f_{α_i} ≡ 1 and the Key Lemma applies.

items.name: Twisted Higgs bundles, their moduli and the Hitchin map
items.statement: Let X → S be a smooth proper family of connected genus-g curves over a Noetherian scheme S, D a line bundle on X, L a line bundle of degree d. A D-Higgs bundle is (E, θ) with E a vector bundle on X and θ : E → E ⊗ D O_X-linear. M^d_{GL_n}(X) is the moduli of stable D-Higgs bundles of rank n and degree d; M^L_{SL_n}(X) that of stable (E, θ) with det E ≅ L and Tr θ = 0. The Hitchin base A is the affine S-space of ⊕_{i=2}^n H⁰(X, D^{⊗i}) (⊕_{i=1}^n for GL_n) and χ sends θ to its characteristic polynomial.
items.locator: §7.1, Definition 7.1 and the paragraph before Theorem 7.6, pp. 575–577
items.note: ET.2b plans the stack of G-bundles with Higgs fields twisted by a sufficiently positive divisor, the Hitchin base and map, over a curve over a finite field. The stable loci, their coarse spaces and the passage to a general Noetherian base are the next items. Definition 7.1(a) prints 'vector bundle on S' for 'on X' (sourceIssues).

items.name: Existence and smoothness of the SL_n Higgs moduli space
items.statement: M^L_{SL_n}(X) is an algebraic space: Bun_n(X/S) is algebraic (Olsson's Hom-stacks), Higgs_D(X/S) → Bun_n(X/S) is representable and affine (EGA II 7.7.6), stable objects are open, and G_m-rigidification preserves algebraicity (Remark 7.2). If D ⊗ (Ω¹_{X/S})^{−1} has strictly positive degree or is O_{X/S}, then M^L_{SL_n}(X/S) is smooth over S (Lemma 7.3).
items.note: Deformations are governed by C^•(E, θ) = [End_0(E) → End_0(E) ⊗ D] in degrees −1, 0 (Ngô 4.14); H⁰ vanishes by stability, and Serre duality identifies H² with trace-free Higgs maps (E, θ) → (E ⊗ D^{−1} ⊗ Ω¹, θ), which vanish by stability and degree.

items.name: PGL_n Higgs moduli stacks and the Γ-action
items.statement: Let Γ = J_X[n] be the n-torsion of the Jacobian. M_{PGL_n}(X/S) is the moduli stack of families of PGL_n-Higgs bundles which are presentable by a stable Higgs bundle over each geometric point; M^d_{PGL_n} is the part presentable by bundles of degree ≡ d mod n (Definition 7.4). M_{PGL_n} = ⊔_{d ∈ Z/n} M^d_{PGL_n}, and M^d_{PGL_n} ≃ [M^L_{SL_n}(X)/Γ] with Γ acting by tensoring, depending only on d mod n (Remark 7.5).

items.name: Properness of the Hitchin map
items.statement: If d and n are coprime, the Hitchin maps χ_{SL_n} : M^L_{SL_n}(X/S) → A and χ_{PGL_n} : M^d_{PGL_n}(X/S) → A are proper.
items.note: Hitchin, Nitsure (GL_n Higgs bundles) and Faltings (G-Higgs bundles for reductive G). ET.2b proves properness only for its anisotropic quotient.

items.name: Changing the determinant is twisting by a torsor
items.statement: Let S = Spec O_F, M a degree-0 line bundle on X and n prime to the residue characteristic. The Kummer sequence of [n] : J_X → J_X gives δ : J_X(O_F) → H¹_ur(F, Γ), δ(M) = [n]^{−1}(M), and M^{LM}_{SL_n}(X) ≃ (M^L_{SL_n}(X))_{δ(M)}.
items.note: Over O_{F^ur}, M has an n-th root and tensoring with it identifies the two spaces; the descent obstruction is δ(M).

items.name: Smooth Hitchin fibres as norm preimages
items.statement: Let π : Y → X × A be the universal spectral curve, A^♦ ⊂ A the locus of smooth spectral curves, and P = P_{SL_n} the relative Prym variety. For a ∈ A^♦(S): (a) χ^{−1}(a) is naturally Nm^{−1}_{Y×_A S/X}(L ⊗ det(π_*O_{Y×_A S})) (as printed); (b) this is an equivalence of P_a-torsors; (c) [Nm^{−1}(M_1)]·[Nm^{−1}(M_2)] = [Nm^{−1}(M_1M_2)] in H¹_ét(S, P); (d) [Nm^{−1}(M^n)] = 0 for M ∈ Pic(X).
items.note: Uses Nm(L′) = det(π_*L′)·det(π_*O)^{−1} (Hausel–Pauly, Corollary 3.12) and multiplicativity of the norm. The formula in (a) has the wrong sign of det(π_*O) (sourceIssues).

items.name: Duality of the SL_n and PGL_n Pryms
items.statement: Define P_{PGL_n} = P_{SL_n}/Γ (Definition 7.9). Over A^♦ there is an isomorphism (P^♦_{SL_n})^∨ ≅ P^♦_{PGL_n} of abelian A^♦-schemes for which the quotient map P^♦_{SL_n} → P^♦_{PGL_n} is a self-dual isogeny, and the induced identification Γ ≅ Γ^∨ of (12) is the one attached to the self-dual isogeny [n] : J_X → J_X (Proposition 7.10).
items.note: After Hausel–Pauly, Lemmas 2.2–2.3; the self-duality is proved with Hom(−, BG_m) on abelian group stacks, applied to Γ → P_{SL_n} → P_{PGL_n}, using that Nm and π^* are dual and that P_{PGL_n} is the cofibre of π^* : J → J̃. It is the SL_n case of the duality of Pryms that PAPER-GROECHENIG-WYSS-ZIEGLER-20-B routes to EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparisonPartII.

items.name: The regular locus of the SL_n and PGL_n Higgs moduli
items.statement: There are natural open dense subspaces M^L_{SL_n}(X)′ ⊂ M^L_{SL_n}(X) and M^d_{PGL_n}(X)′ ⊂ M^d_{PGL_n}(X) on which P_{SL_n} and P_{PGL_n} act faithfully and transitively, with complements of codimension ≥ 2 (Proposition 7.11). If Γ is constant over S, then (M^L_{SL_n}, P_{SL_n}, A) and (M^d_{PGL_n}, P_{PGL_n}, A) are abstract Hitchin systems (Proposition 7.12).
items.note: Ngô, Proposition 4.3.3, and reference [42], Theorem 2.1. The regular locus as a torsor under the regular centraliser is planned in ET.2b over finite fields; the codimension bound and the stable SL_n/PGL_n forms are not.

items.name: Torsor calculus for SL_n Hitchin fibres
items.statement: For a ∈ A^♦(S) write P^0_a = (P_{SL_n})_a, P^L_a = (M^L_{SL_n})_a and M = det(π_*O_Y). (a) P^L_a·P^{L′}_a ≃ P^{LL′M^{−1}}_a; (b) (P^L_a)^d ≃ P^{L^dM^{−d+1}}_a; (c) P^L_a ≃ P^{LN^n}_a for N ∈ Pic(X) (Lemma 7.13). If F is a local field of residue characteristic p > n, X a curve over O_F and a ∈ A^♦(F) extends to an O_F-point, then the order of P^L_a in H¹(F, P^0_a) divides n (Lemma 7.14).
items.note: The proof of Lemma 7.13 identifies P^L_a with Nm^{−1}(LM) and derives P^{LL′M}, the opposite sign to the statement; the statement is the correct one (sourceIssues).

items.name: Independence of the degree for GL_n Higgs point counts
items.statement: Let n, d be positive coprime integers, k a finite field of characteristic p prime to n and d, X/k a smooth proper curve of genus g, and D a line bundle with D ⊗ (Ω¹_X)^{−1} of strictly positive even degree or equal to O_X; assume k contains a primitive n^{2g}-th root of unity. Then #M^d_{GL_n}(X)(k) = #M^e_{GL_n}(X)(k) for every integer e prime to n and p. (Theorem 1.7 of the introduction; the coprime, independence-of-d part of Mozgovoy–Schiffmann's conjecture.)
items.note: Lift to O_F, compare p-adic volumes via Weil's formula and Fubini over A_{GL_n}(O_F)^♭; the order of each fibre torsor divides n, so for d, e prime to n one fibre has an F-point iff the other does. Also proved by Yu (automorphic) and, without coprimality, by Mellit.

items.name: Independence of the degree for SL_n Higgs point counts
items.statement: Let n, d be positive coprime integers, k a finite field of characteristic p > n, X/k a smooth proper genus-g curve with D ⊗ (Ω¹_X)^{−1} of strictly positive even degree or O_X, L of degree d, and k containing a primitive n^{2g}-th root of unity. There is a degree-0 line bundle N on X with #M^L_{SL_n}(X)(k) = #M^{L^eN^{e−1}}_{SL_n}(X)(k) for every e prime to n (Theorem 7.16). Over C, the Betti and Hodge numbers of M^L_{SL_n}(X) and M^d_{GL_n}(X) are independent of d (Corollary 7.17).
items.note: vol(M^L_{SL_n}(O_F)) = ∫_{A(O_F)^♭} (∫_{P^0_a(F)} δ_{P^L_a}|ω_a|)|η|; δ_{(P^L_a)^e} = δ_{P^L_a} by Lemma 7.14, (P^L_a)^e ≃ P^{L^eM^{e−1}}_a by Lemma 7.13 (sign as printed), and N = M·Q^{−n} with deg Q^n = deg M, which exists because deg M = −(deg D)n(n−1)/2 is divisible by n when deg D is even.

items.name: The Hausel–Thaddeus gerbes
items.statement: Let S = Spec R with n invertible, n and d coprime, Γ = Pic⁰(X)[n] constant and μ_{n·|Γ|} = μ_{n^{2g+1}} constant over R. The μ_n-gerbe α_{SL_n,L} on M^L_{SL_n}(X) is the obstruction to a universal family, represented by the stack 𝕄^L_{SL_n}(X) of stable L-twisted SL_n-Higgs bundles over its rigidification M^L_{SL_n}(X); it is Γ-equivariant and descends to α_{PGL_n,L} on M^d_{PGL_n}(X) = [M^L_{SL_n}(X)/Γ]. For e ≥ 1 prime to n, e′ = ad ≡ e mod n and L′ = L^a, this gives α_{SL_n,L′} and α_{PGL_n,L′} on M^e_{PGL_n}.
items.note: Hausel–Thaddeus §3 over C; the paper applies it over R 'with minor modifications'.

items.name: Hausel–Thaddeus: the Higgs gerbes are dual
items.statement: α_{SL_n,L} and α_{PGL_n,L′} are arithmetic, and there are canonical isomorphisms Split′((M^L_{SL_n})^♦/A^♦, α^e_{SL_n,L}) ≃ (M^e_{PGL_n})^♦ of P^♦_{PGL_n}-torsors and Split′((M^e_{PGL_n})^♦/A^♦, α^d_{PGL_n,L′}) ≃ (M^L_{SL_n})^♦ of P^♦_{SL_n}-torsors.
items.note: Hausel–Thaddeus, Propositions 3.2 and 3.6, applied mutatis mutandis; their Triv is Split′.

items.name: The SL_n and PGL_n Higgs moduli form a dual pair
items.statement: (Lemma 7.19) For R = O_F satisfying the standing assumptions and a ∈ A(O_F) ∩ A^♦(F), χ_{SL_n}^{−1}(a_F) and χ_{PGL_n}^{−1}(a_F) both have F-points iff α^e_{SL_n,L} and α^d_{PGL_n,L′} both split on them. (Proposition 7.20) (M^L_{SL_n}, P_{SL_n}, A) and (M^e_{PGL_n}, P_{PGL_n}, A) with α^e_{SL_n,L} and α^d_{PGL_n,L′} form a dual pair of abstract Hitchin systems over R.
items.note: 'Only if': F-points make Split′ trivial, so by Lemma 6.5 the gerbes are constant on the fibres; on the SL_n side an F-point extends to an O_F-point by properness and Br(O_F) = 0; on the PGL_n side the SL^e_n fibre is a power of the SL^d_n fibre (Lemma 7.13), so it has an O_F-point whose image works.

items.name: Topological mirror symmetry for SL_n and PGL_n Higgs bundles
items.statement: Let X be a smooth projective genus-g curve over a field k with D ⊗ (Ω¹_X)^{−1} of strictly positive even degree or O_X, n ≥ 1, d and e prime to n, L ∈ Pic^d(X), and k containing a primitive root of unity of order n^{2g+1}. (a) If k = C: E(M^L_{SL_n}(X); x, y) = E_st(M^e_{PGL_n}(X), α^d_{PGL_n,L′}; x, y). (b) If k = F_q with p > n: #M^L_{SL_n}(X)(k) = #^{α^d_{PGL_n,L′}}_st(M^e_{PGL_n}(X)). (Theorem 1.1 of the introduction, conjectured by Hausel–Thaddeus.)
items.note: (a): spread out to R ⊂ C of finite type containing 1/n and the n^{2g+1}-th roots of unity, make Γ constant by an étale extension and apply Theorem 6.11; the stringy E-polynomial of the smooth scheme M^L_{SL_n} with the gerbe is its E-polynomial. (b): Theorem 6.12.

items.name: Consequences: Hodge numbers and fibrewise Galois representations
items.statement: (Corollary 7.22) For k = C and D = Ω¹_X: h^{p,q}_c(M^L_{SL_n}(X)) = h^{p,q}_{c,st}(M^e_{PGL_n}(X), α^d_{PGL_n,L′}). (Theorem 7.23) For k finite of characteristic p > n satisfying the standing assumptions and every a ∈ A(k), the Gal(k)-representations (Rχ_{SL_n,*}Q̄_ℓ)_a and (R(Iχ_{PGL_n})_*N_{L′}(F_{PGL_n}))_a are abstractly isomorphic.
items.note: 7.22 uses purity of both cohomologies for D = Ω¹ (Hausel–Thaddeus §6). 7.23 uses purity of both complexes (properness, Verdier duality, Deligne's Weil II, stratum by stratum on the inertia stack) and the fibrewise point counts of Theorem 6.12.

items.name: The Γ-isotypic parts of the SL_n cohomology
items.statement: Let k be a finite field containing all n^{2g+1}-th roots of unity with a primitive n-th root ζ and Γ constant; the self-dual isogeny [n] of J_X gives Γ ≅ Γ^∨ and, with ζ, a non-degenerate pairing (,) : Γ × Γ → μ_n(k) ≅ Z/n ⊂ Q/Z. With X, D, d, e as in Theorem 7.21, L ∈ Pic^d(X) and L′ a power of L of degree ≡ e mod n: for γ ∈ Γ and χ ∈ Γ^* corresponding under (,), Tr(Fr, H^*_c(M^L_{SL_n}(X), Q̄_ℓ)_χ) = Tr(Fr, H^*_c([(M^{L′}_{SL_n}(X))^γ/Γ], N_{L′}(F_{PGL_n}))). (A form of Hausel's conjecture.)
items.note: Fourier transform over Γ of both sides of Theorem 7.21(b): twists M^{[ν]}_{SL_n} by ν ∈ Γ ≅ Pic⁰(X)(k)/Pic⁰(X)(k)^n have Frobenius ν^{−1}∘Fr (Proposition 4.8), and Lemma 7.25 gives the PGL_n side.

items.name: The twisted sectors change by the Weil pairing
items.note: With A = P_{SL_n,a_F} and B = A/Γ, the sequence 0 → Γ → A(F) → B(F) →β H¹(F, Γ) →α H¹(F, A) → … is self-dual (Lemma 3.15, Proposition 7.10), so ⟨α(T), b⟩ = ⟨T, β(b)⟩_Γ; T_{L_2} = α(ν)·T_{L_1}; each side is a p-adic integral of f_{α_{L_i}} (Corollary 5.29), described by Lemma 6.7, and ⟨ν, β(b)⟩_Γ = (ν, γ′) by Lemma 3.7 because ν is unramified and e(b) lies in the γ′-sector.
